reports.title: TAPESTRY, INC. REPORTS FISCAL 2027 FIRST QUARTER RESULTS AND RAISES FULL YEAR OUTLOOK

guidance.heading: Financial Outlook
section: Tapestry is raising its Fiscal 2027 outlook, which is provided on a non-GAAP and comparable 52-week versus 52-week basis:

desk.headline: Sales up 11% to $1.9bn, adjusted EPS $1.82 beat; full-year sales and EPS outlook raised
results: Sales rose 11% to $1.89bn (12% excluding the sold Stuart Weitzman brand), led by Coach up 16%; Kate Spade fell 10%.
Growth was broad: Greater China +39%, Europe +22% and North America +4% in constant currency.
Adjusted gross margin widened 2.2 pts to 78.7% on efficiencies, lower tariffs and currency; adjusted operating income rose 24% to $439m.
Adjusted EPS jumped 32% to $1.82, well ahead of the $1.56 estimate; GAAP EPS was $1.76.
About $700m was returned in the quarter, including $600m of buybacks (about 4.6m shares at $130 average).

guidance.summary: Tapestry raised its fiscal 2027 outlook: sales of $8.5-8.6bn (was $8.4-8.5bn), adjusted EPS of $8.25-8.35 (was $7.80-7.90) and about 1 pt of operating margin expansion (was about 0.5 pts). Buybacks were lifted to $1.7bn and total returns to about $2.0bn. For Q2 it expects 5-6% constant-currency sales growth and EPS of about $3.05.

points: Management sees a clear path for Coach to become a $10bn brand; Coach grew 41% in Greater China and 7% in North America.
Coach is leaning on scarcity rather than discounts, focusing on $200-500 handbags and cutting cheaper promotional units.
Kate Spade is expected to fall by high single digits this year with a small operating loss while its turnaround continues.
Lower tariffs added about 0.7 pts to gross margin; the outlook assumes a low-to-mid-20% US tariff rate.
US shoppers were described as discerning but resilient, with growth across age and income groups.
